name: medicine and neurology overview
title: Neurological problems from other systems: cancer (five mechanisms, including checkpoint inhibitor autoimmunity), breathlessness from bilateral phrenic nerve palsies, thiamine deficiency (Wernicke encephalopathy), other nutritional syndromes and refeeding, and multiple cardioembolic strokes from endocarditis; each column gives presentation, investigations and management

root.title: A neurological problem in a medically ill patient: how is the illness reaching the nervous system?
lines: localize first, as for any weakness: muscle · neuromuscular junction · nerve · root · anterior horn cell · spinal cord · brain

head: h
Five ways cancer reaches the nerves
pres: • paraneoplastic antibodies: limbic encephalitis, dermatomyositis, myasthenia gravis, cerebellitis
ptosis, neck and proximal weakness, normal reflexes and sensation
tx: With oncology: STOP the inhibitor and/or STEROIDS

head: h
Bilateral phrenic nerve palsies
weak diaphragm
pres: • normal heart, chest, limbs, cranial nerves
~lying down the diaphragm does the work; upright, the intercostals

head: h
Thiamine (B1) deficiency: Wernicke encephalopathy
inv: Will not localize to one place
tx: give it BEFORE glucose if nutrition is in doubt

head: h
Other nutrition
pres: • B1: dry beriberi = neuropathy · wet = cardiomyopathy
inv: after long starvation, electrolytes shift into cells: ↓ sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, phosphate

head: h
Multiple cardioembolic strokes
atrial fibrillation · endocarditis (infective, cancer, Libman-Sacks) · cardiac tumours
pres: Deficits in SEVERAL territories, ACUTE and STEPWISE
• splinter hemorrhages, Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, Roth spots
